title: Sweden gave the public access to official records in 1766
body: Sweden's first Freedom of the Press Act was introduced in 1766. Along with restricting censorship, it established a principle of public access to documents produced by the authorities.
takeaway: Freedom to publish is easier to exercise when the information needed to scrutinise government is available.
source: Sveriges Riksdag, The Development of Constitutional Law in Sweden
visual: an open wooden archive drawer holding bundles of blank-backed papers

title: Singapore's Parliament includes appointed members
body: A parliamentary committee in Singapore can nominate up to nine people for appointment by the president as Nominated Members of Parliament. Their term is two and a half years.
takeaway: Appointment adds a route into the chamber distinct from winning an electoral district.
source: Parliament of Singapore, Special Select Committee and Educational Resources
visual: a semicircle of empty chairs in a modern parliamentary chamber

title: A permanent UN member can abstain without using its veto
body: Substantive decisions of the UN Security Council require at least nine votes in favour. A negative vote by a permanent member blocks such a decision. An abstention by that member does not, if the vote has enough support.
takeaway: A member can decline to endorse a resolution while letting the other votes decide its fate.
source: United Nations Security Council, Voting System
